bib.title: More Agents Is All You Need

question: Does the performance of LLMs scale with the number of agents (independent samples) instantiated under a simple sampling-and-voting method, and when does it hold?
hypothesis: LLM performance may likely be improved by a brute-force scaling up of the number of agents instantiated, with larger gains on harder tasks and weaker models.
contributions: First systematic study on the scaling property of raw agents instantiated by LLMs: performance scales with the number of agents using simple sampling and voting.
Explore compatibility of the method with existing complicated methods, showing it enhances them further.
Analyse effectiveness across problem difficulty and distil properties, from which Step-wise and Hierarchical Agent Forest are proposed.

method.summary: Agent Forest: feed the same query (alone or wrapped in a prompting or multi-agent method) to an LLM N times, then pick the sample with highest cumulative similarity to the others (frequency for closed-ended tasks, BLEU for code). Evaluated on five benchmarks with Llama2-13B/70B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo, alone and stacked on CoT, ZS-CoT, SPP, Debate and Reflection.
method.task: Arithmetic reasoning, general reasoning and code generation via sampling-and-voting ensembles

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.preprocessing: Answers extracted by matching boxed{X}; mathematical-equivalence comparison for voting and scoring

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.preprocessing: Answer extracted by matching '(X' or '(X)' with X in A-D; vote by option frequency

datasets.name: Chess state tracking (BIG-bench)
datasets.source: Chess State Tracking task, used by Du et al. 2023 and Zhang et al. 2023
datasets.preprocessing: Answer is a chessboard position matched with the same pattern; vote by frequency

datasets.name: HumanEval
datasets.preprocessing: Python snippets extracted from responses; vote by cumulative sacreBLEU

datasets.name: Synthetic interval task (Sec 6.1)
datasets.source: Constructed by authors: find interval Delta_k containing sum_{i=1..S} a_i*b_i, a_i,b_i random integers in [-I,I], K equal-probability intervals

other.version: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 for Sec 4-5; gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 with JSON mode for Sec 6
gpt-4-0613 in Table 2 (single query only); gpt4-1106-Preview in JSON mode in Sec 6

inference.decoding: Independent repeated sampling from the same prompt; final answer by majority vote (frequency) or highest cumulative BLEU similarity
inference.temperature: Default T = 1.0 (varied in robustness ablation, Fig 4)
inference.top_p: Default p = 1.0 (varied in robustness ablation, Fig 4)
inference.samples: Ensemble size up to 40, averaged over 10 independent runs (20 runs for the T/p ablation; 10 runs for Sec 6); Debate integration capped at ensemble size 10
inference.prompting: Single query, CoT, Zero-shot CoT, SPP, or multi-agent Debate and Reflection wrappers; prompt texts not given

parameters.similarity: occurrence frequency for closed-ended tasks; sacreBLEU for HumanEval

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of items where the voted answer matches ground truth (HumanEval reported as accuracy in the same tables)

metrics.name: Relative performance gain eta
metrics.definition: (Pm - Ps)/Ps with Pm accuracy with the method and Ps with a single query

metrics.name: Average rank
metrics.definition: Average rank each method+Ours achieves across all five tasks for a given LLM, from Table 3

metrics.name: Tokens per sample
metrics.definition: Token usage for a single agent

eval.protocol: Mean over 10 independent runs with standard error; one-way ANOVA across ensemble sizes (1,10,20,30,40) on 10 runs, all p<0.05.

evidence.quote: the effectiveness of our method is evaluated by averaging the results across 10 independent runs. During each run, we scale up the ensemble size to 40 to ensure maximum gains. However, when integrating our method with the Debate Du et al. (2023), the ensemble size is limited to 10

results.claim: Sampling-and-voting with ensemble 40 raises GSM8K accuracy by 12% to 24% across Llama2-13B, Llama2-70B and GPT-3.5-Turbo.
results.setup: GSM8K, Llama2-13B/70B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613, ensemble size 40 vs a single query, 10 runs
results.quote: the accuracy gains range from 12% to 24% on the GSM8K and from 6% to 10% on the MATH.

results.claim: MATH gain range with ensemble 40 is 6% to 10%.
results.setup: MATH, same three models, ensemble 40, 10 runs
results.quote: the accuracy gains range from 12% to 24% on the GSM8K and from 6% to 10% on the MATH.

results.claim: Chess gain range is 1% to 4% and MMLU gain range is 5% to 11%.
results.setup: Chess state tracking and MMLU, same three models, ensemble 40, 10 runs
results.quote: In general reasoning tasks, the accuracy gains range from 1% to 4% on the Chess and from 5% to 11% on the MMLU.

results.claim: HumanEval gain range is 4% to 9% with BLEU-based voting.
results.setup: HumanEval, same three models, ensemble 40, 10 runs
results.quote: In code generation task, the accuracy gains range from 4% to 9% on HumanEval.

results.claim: Llama2-13B with ensemble-40 voting beats a single Llama2-70B query on GSM8K.
results.setup: GSM8K, Llama2-13B with Agent Forest (40) vs Llama2-70B single query
results.quote: the enhanced Llama2-13B model achieves 59% accuracy on the GSM8K dataset, outperforming the Llama2-70B model, which scores 54%.
results.note: Table 2 prints 0.59 +/- 5e-4 (13B Ours) and 0.54 +/- 3e-2 (70B Single). Fig 1 caption says 13B reaches comparable accuracy to 70B at ensemble size 15.

results.claim: Voting alone has the best average rank (2.5 overall) against CoT, ZS-CoT, SPP, Debate and Reflection each stacked with voting.
results.setup: Ranks derived from Table 3 across five tasks per LLM. Samples: voting methods at ensemble 40 (Debate at 10), 10 runs. Overall ranks: CoT+Ours 3.3, ZS-CoT+Ours 2.7, SPP+Ours 4, Debate+Ours 4.4, Reflection+Ours 3.3, Ours 2.5.
results.table: Table 4, row Ours, column Overall (2.6, 2.6, 2.2, 2.5 for GPT-3.5, 70B, 13B, Overall)
results.note: Table 4 header is 'Method +Ours'. The text says the ranking is of each enhanced method, which means the rows other than 'Ours' are the other method plus voting. Ensemble size per method in the rank comparison is not stated separately beyond the global 40 (10 for Debate).

results.claim: Voting alone outperforms the other methods used standalone in most cases except Chess with Llama2-13B and 70B.
results.setup: Table 3 standalone columns vs Ours row, ensemble 40, 10 runs
results.quote: our method outperforms other methods in standalone cases, except on the Chess task using Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B.

results.claim: Stacking voting on Debate gives HumanEval scores of 0 for both Llama2 models (standalone also 0).
results.setup: HumanEval, Debate standalone vs Debate+Ours, Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B; Debate ensemble capped at 10
results.quote: two notable exceptions are observed when integrated with the debate method with the Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B models, which result in failed cases.
results.table: Table 3, rows Debate (Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B), HumanEval columns Standalone and +Ours: 0 and 0
results.note: Authors attribute the failure to noise from referencing other agents' answers breaking code coherence; untested. GPT-3.5 Debate HumanEval is 0.56 -> 0.67 (+0.11).

results.claim: Gains from stacking voting on other methods: 10% to 21% GSM8K, 1% to 15% MATH, 1% to 13% Chess, 1% to 11% MMLU, 2% to 7% HumanEval.
results.setup: Table 3, CoT/ZS-CoT/SPP/Debate/Reflection standalone vs +Ours across three LLMs
results.quote: yielding increases between 10% and 21% on the GSM8K dataset, and between 1% and 15% on the MATH dataset.
results.note: Table 3 has larger cell gains (e.g. SPP Llama2-70B GSM8K +0.27, Reflection +0.25), and Debate GPT-3.5 GSM8K +0.02, so the quoted ranges do not match the table extremes.

results.claim: Relative gain is larger with harder tasks and weaker models.
results.setup: Computed from Table 2; GSM8K (easy) 69/37/16 and MATH (hard) 200/120/34 for Llama2-13B/70B/GPT-3.5
results.quote: the smaller model, Llama2-13B, gains ranging from 28%-200%, but only 8%-16% over GPT-3.5-Turbo.
results.note: Large relative gains on MATH come from tiny bases (0.03 to 0.09).

results.claim: Inherent-difficulty property: gains rise then fall as integer range I grows.
results.setup: Synthetic task, GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106, I from 10 to 400, 40 samples vs 1
results.quote: The most notable gains are seen at I = 100 and I = 200, consistent across all S and K settings.

results.claim: Step-wise Agent Forest gives 15%-42% gains on the synthetic task, rising with inherent difficulty.
results.setup: Synthetic task, S=8, K=4, I from 100 to 400, GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106
results.quote: Figure 7 (middle) shows that compared to Agent Forest, Step-wise Agent Forest yields greater improvements.
results.note: The 15%-42% figure is in the following sentence ('e.g., we see 15%-42% gains').

results.claim: Hierarchical Agent Forest with GPT-3.5 at K=8 then GPT-4 at K=32 raises accuracy from 35% to 47%; homogeneous GPT-3.5 from 21% to 31%.
results.setup: Synthetic task K=32; heterogeneous GPT-3.5-Turbo then GPT-4 vs GPT-4 alone at K=32
results.quote: compared with the result of GPT-4 with K = 32, the hierarchical method improves performance from 35% to 47%

results.claim: Accuracy gains are significant across ensemble sizes for all model-task pairs (one-way ANOVA).
Token usage grows proportionally with the number of agents; single-agent GPT-3.5 tokens are 235 (GSM8K) to 495 (HumanEval).
results.quote: the token usage increases proportionally with the number of agents or when combined with other methods.
results.table: Table 5, row Ours (single agent), column GSM8K: 235 +/- 54

limits: Authors concede cost: token usage grows proportionally with ensemble size and optimisation is left to future work.
Debate integration capped at ensemble size 10 because of communication overhead, versus 40 for other methods, so rank comparisons are not at equal sample counts.
Gains taper off at extreme difficulty (I=400) and are small for Chess (+1 to +4).
Models are Llama2 and GPT-3.5/GPT-4 from 2023; no modern reasoning models. GPT-4 evaluated only as a single query.
'Agents' are independent samples of the same prompt with no interaction or roles.
Debate failure on HumanEval is attributed to noise but untested.
Dataset sizes, max tokens and prompt texts are not stated; Table 3 gains do not exactly match the quoted ranges.
Voting needs an extractable or comparable answer; code relies on BLEU similarity.

terms.definition: Two-phase sampling-and-voting method: generate N samples from an LLM or LLM-agent framework, then pick the one with highest cumulative similarity.
Decompose the task into steps, apply Agent Forest to each step in turn and use the result to update the task.
Decompose low-prior-probability tasks into higher-probability subtasks solved hierarchically, possibly with different models.
